summary: Request: compact ordered audit sample (SQL-ready) + column crosswalk and SOC2 evidence checklist
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a compact, chronologically ordered audit export (CSV/NDJSON) that is SQL-ready with a detailed column crosswalk mapping Redwood audit fields to common relational columns. They also request a SOC2-oriented evidence checklist showing how the export satisfies logging retention, ordering, tamper-evidence, and per-tenant pseudonymization requirements.

Impact: Customer (Aurelia Payments) needs the dataset for an imminent SOC2 audit in two weeks. Without a curated sample and a field-to-column mapping, their auditors cannot validate retention and event provenance. This is time-sensitive for contract renewal.

Environment: production account (customer-managed VPC). Region: eu-west. Export target: S3 presigned bundle.

Requested deliverables: 1) One compact CSV sample (max 10k rows) covering a 24-hour window across March 1, 2026, UTC, 2) SQL-ready column crosswalk (CSV header -> SQL column types and sample SELECT statements), 3) SOC2 evidence checklist (which fields prove retention, ordering, non-repudiation, HMAC manifest), 4) Playbook notes for timezone normalization and resume tokens for auditors to replay events.

Customer-provided context: They require deterministic ordering (UTC timeline), per-row HMAC or checksum, pseudonymized user IDs (reversible by escrow) and a mapping that shows which fields contain PII and how redaction/pseudonymization was applied.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Support console -> Exports -> New Export -> Select 'Audit: compact sample' template.
2) Select time range 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-01T23:59:59Z, set region eu-west, output format CSV with headers.
3) Choose 'pseudonymize' = reversible (HSM-backed) and 'include_hmac_manifest' = true.
4) Request via API: POST /v1/admin/exports with body {"template":"compact-audit-sample", "params":{"start":...}} and await S3 presigned URL.

Expected: single CSV file in S3 named aurelia-sample-20260301.csv plus aurelia-sample-20260301.manifest.json (manifest contains HMACs and resume token). Rows ordered by event_timestamp_utc ascending and timezone normalized to UTC.

Observed: Support generated a sample but observed timestamps in some rows use local timezone offsets (CEST) for events around 2026-03-01T01:00:00+01:00 which causes ordering anomalies. Manifest HMAC present.
logs:
Export job id: export-6f9b2c (generated 2026-03-12T18:02:13Z). S3 object: s3://redwood-aurelia-exports/prod/eu-west/export-6f9b2c/aurelia-sample-20260301.csv. Manifest: s3://.../aurelia-sample-20260301.manifest.json.
Sample row excerpt (CSV): "event_id,event_timestamp,event_type,tenant_id,user_id,payload"
"e-9f3a,2026-03-01T02:15:00+01:00,model.request,t-443,uid-XXXX,{...}"
Hash verification: manifest.hmacs[e-9f3a] = OK. Ordering check: row 18 timestamp 2026-03-01T00:58:00Z appears after row 19 timestamp 2026-03-01T01:05:00+01:00 when interpreted naively (string sort).
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduced export in support tenant and observed mixed timestamp representations (some events stored with timezone offsets preserved; others normalized to Z). Root cause hypothesis: ingestion-time metadata included original event timezone and our export pipeline conditionally preserved offsets when source_event.tz present. 2) Manifest generation uses canonical UTC conversion for HMAC inputs, so HMACs are consistent even when CSV shows offsets. 3) Ordering anomalies stem from consumers doing lexicographic sort on the textual timestamp instead of parsing ISO offset. 4) Immediate workaround: regenerate export with explicit parameter `normalize_timestamps_to_utc=true`. This was tested and produced uniformly Z-suffixed timestamps. 5) Engineering follow-up: add schema-version header and explicit `timestamp_normalization` flag to export API to prevent implicit behavior.
comments:
Support (Marco Lopez) 2026-03-12: "We ran the export and confirmed manifest HMACs verify. Ordering anomalies due to mixed timestamp formats — recommending UTC normalization flag."

Customer (Elena Martinez, Aurelia) 2026-03-13: "Thanks — can you also include a SQL snippet that shows how an auditor can deduplicate by event_id and reconstitute ordering using the resume_token?"

Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-13: "Planned: attach SQL-ready crosswalk and two sample queries (one for ordering/dedup, one for PII mapping). ETA for attachments: 2026-03-14 EOD. Engineering ticket to standardize export header created (INT-33099)."
resolution:
Workaround delivered: regenerated an export with `normalize_timestamps_to_utc=true` and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-aurelia-exports/prod/eu-west/export-6f9b2c/normalized/aurelia-sample-20260301.csv and corresponding manifest. Provided SQL-ready crosswalk (attached as CSV) and sample queries: 1) ORDER BY event_timestamp_utc, 2) dedupe using ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY event_timestamp_utc DESC). Provided SOC2 evidence checklist mapping: retention_policy->retention.metadata, ordering->manifest.resume_token, non-repudiation->manifest.hmacs, pseudonymization->pseudonymization.key_id & rotation statements.

Follow-ups: Engineering task INT-33099 to add export header `x-export-schema-version: 2026-03-14-v1` and API param `timestamp_normalization` (assigned to infra team). Security requested HSM attestation documents — escalated to Security Ops (SEC-1018).

Case status: Deliverables provided to customer; awaiting auditor confirmation. Keep ticket open until auditor signs off or until 2026-03-18, at which point we'll follow up.
